name: security/github_oauth.py: client_secret is logged and sent in the URL query string
description:
REAL finding (not a scanner false positive), found while auditing the CISO package for the secrets-resolver increment. It is out of scope for that task, so it is recorded here.

## Evidence (api/codx/junior/security/github_oauth.py)
- L61 `logger.info("get_access_token %s", data)` — `data` contains `client_secret` and `code_verifier`, so the OAuth client secret is written to the container log on every login.
- L62-63 `query_string = "&".join(...)` then `requests.post(f"{token_url}?{query_string}")` — `client_secret` is placed in the URL QUERY STRING (not the body). It therefore also lands in: proxy/access logs, `err.request.url` which L67-70 logs via `logger.exception`, any tracing/APM capture, and the browser/HTTP history.
- Note: the CISO audit flagged this file at L50 (`secret.hardcoded-credential`) which is a FALSE positive (a URL literal). The real defect at L61-L63 was not flagged.

## What to do
1. Send the token exchange as a POST *body* (`requests.post(token_url, data=data, headers={"Accept": "application/json"})`), never in the query string.
2. Delete the `logger.info(... data ...)` line; if a log is needed, log only the grant type and a truncated `code` digest (see `redact_token` in `codx/junior/security/user_management.py`).
3. Never log `err.request.url` for this request; log the status code and a request id instead.
4. Rotate the GitHub OAuth client secret for every deployment that has already run this code — treat it as disclosed in logs.

## Acceptance criteria
- No `client_secret` value can appear in any log record from this module (add a test that captures `caplog` during `get_access_token` and asserts the secret is absent).
- The token exchange request carries no credentials in the request line.
- `security_audit` on `api/codx/junior/security/github_oauth.py` reports 0 findings above `low`.
